entries.title: Romans 14:1
segments: Decision of scruples. The believer whose faith was weak was to be made to feel that differences with the church authorities on minor points should not be allowed to prejudice him, provided he held the essential truths of the gospel.  In this chapter the apostle considers the doubts of some Christians in regard to food and other matters. This was necessary only because they were weak in faith, and if their scruples were not judiciously dealt with they might desert their stronger brethren.  These latter were too well established in the faith to be troubled with doubts on comparatively unimportant questions.

entries.title: Romans 14:9
segments: Lord of both the dead and the living. Master of the believer both on earth and in heaven.

entries.title: Romans 14:10
segments: Why dost thou judge thy brother? Why dost thou judge thy brother, when thou knowest that thou also shalt be judged?

entries.title: Romans 14:15
segments: Thy meat. Thy prejudice about so small a matter as the food a Christian ought to eat.

entries.title: Romans 14:16
segments: Your good. The Christian enlightenment and freedom which make you spiritually strong and useful.

entries.title: Romans 14:17
segments: The kingdom of God. The reign of Christ in the heart in this world and the world to come.

entries.title: Romans 14:22
segments:
Have thou to thyself before God. Be strictly accountable for it to God alone.
 

 
That judgeth not himself. That hath not occasion to rebuke himself for wrong indulgence.
